definition: The reality/land described by Klavis Verge as threatened and as the place where the player guides adventurers.
cultural_caution: A named realm, not a character node or proof of a complete cosmology, geography, or cross-title continuity equivalence.

definition: The manual's term for the moral order: a king who embraces it is worthy to rule, while the Temple of Baa seeks to destroy the pact between gods and earthly rulers.
cultural_caution: This is a source-specific fictional system term. It is not equated with historical or living religious/political traditions of the same English wording.

supports: Definition, kingship connection, and Temple of Baa objective

definition: The doomsday cult the manual says grows more deadly and schemes to destroy the Mandate's pact.
cultural_caution: A collective faction/cult, never a character node or a basis for assigning every individual an alignment.

citations.locator: Printed pp. 6–7, 'King Roland is Missing' and 'The Mandate of Heaven'
supports: Temple of Baa identity, doomsday-cult framing, and stated scheme

definition: The stars the opening says some people use for twisted guidance and associates with the cold terror opposing the Mandate.
cultural_caution: A limited narrative/cosmological phrase; the manual does not warrant a full astronomical or metaphysical taxonomy.

citations.locator: PDF printed pp. 6–7, opening narrative and 'The Mandate of Heaven'
supports: Demon-star phrase, cult guidance, and opposition framing

definition: Klavis Verge's self-applied title in the manual framing.
cultural_caution: A named individual title, not a player class or a claim that all magic-users share a hierarchy.

definition: The exact manual designation for Sulman while he investigates the snowstorms.
cultural_caution: A source-native proficiency/title; its spell list, rank mechanics, elemental ontology, and applicability to other games are not assumed.

citations.locator: PDF printed p. 14, Roland letter dated August 23, 1152
supports: Sulman's Master of Air designation and snowstorm inquiry

definition: Klavis's label for the computer/keyboard/mouse framing instruments by which the player commands actions across worlds.
cultural_caution: A metafictional interface phrase, not evidence that every UI control is a literal in-world artifact or that it transfers unchanged to other releases.

citations.locator: PDF printed p. 17, 'Intro to Mouse & Keyboard Controls'
supports: Exact term and cross-world interface framing

definition: The new-game option that lets the player create party members and change their portrait, name, class, statistics, and skills.
cultural_caution: It establishes player-character variability, so created adventurers are not stable canonical NPC records; it is not a source for a fixed party roster.

citations.locator: Getting Started, p. 1: 'After the introduction sequence' and 'Character Creation'
supports: New Game/Create Party option and editable party-member dimensions

definition: The manual says the starting player party can include four characters drawn from six classes, then describes class selection and advancement.
cultural_caution: Classes are player mechanics/dimensions, not individual characters or a justification for inventing canonical party members.

citations.locator: PDF printed pp. 23–24, 'Intro to Character Creation' and 'Character Creation Info'
supports: Four-character party, six classes, selection, and advancement framing

definition: The getting-started card's label for non-player people who may share information, be hired, or automatically join the party, subject to stated limits.
cultural_caution: A generic gameplay category, not a named collective character or a basis to promote all hirelings to character nodes.

supports: NPC interaction/hiring category and stated follower limits
